title: Pilot Request
description: The frontmatter of a pilot request (XR): a proposed change to the project the pilot puts forward, in plain, clear and simple prose covering the problem, individual request units, risks, and how it is executed and verified. The commander responds with a CR enacting full, part or held approval. Filed by identifier with a dash, XR-015.md.

type.description: the words Pilot Request, which is what chooses this schema

unit.description: this request's identifier, XR, a dash and three digits, the same identifier the file is named for

name.description: one to three words the writer chose for the record's contents, appended to the file name after the id (CA-049)

status.description: draft while the pilot may still remake it, frozen once the commander gives full approval, held while the commander has blocked it from progressing; executed once crew have carried it out, withdrawn if the pilot took it back, superseded if events overtook it

approval.description: the commander's enacted approval: full (the pilot proceeds), part (the commander added to or adjusted their own record, and the pilot redrafts against it), held (blocked from progressing), or empty while still awaiting the commander's word

sections.description: the four sections the body covers, in this fixed order: the problem, the individual request units, the risks, and how it is executed and verified. This only names the sections; the linter does not check the body's own headings

stamp.description: three items: the date as YYYY-MM-DD, who wrote it, and the eight-character session id

context.description: the identifiers this request comes out of, a bracketed list, usually a dossier; an empty list where there is none, since the key is always written so its absence is never a question. The old Rq, P, Or and De forms are accepted only until XD-005's citation sweep replaces them

generates.description: the identifiers of what this request led to, a bracketed list, usually the commander's response and any plan or mission that followed. The old Rq, P, Or and De forms are accepted only until XD-005's citation sweep replaces them
